transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-09
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya (AE), Liam (SE), Noah (CSM) - Redwood; Priya (Procurement), Carlos (Legal), Jodie (CTO), Ben (Security) - Sable Health

Summary:
Quick gatecall to resolve outstanding nonstandard MSA/DPA clauses, confirm SLA credit language, agree pilot acceptance criteria and finalize path to pricing approval. Heavy discussion on KMS/bring-your-own-key, indemnity caps, and data residency for EU patients.

Topics:
- MSA redlines and exceptions
- DPA: data residency & deletion SLA
- SLA credits & uptime definitions
- Pricing approval timeline and PO path
- Pilot scope and technical benchmarking
- Security artifacts and KMS options

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'll kick us off — main goal today is to get clarity on the MSA exceptions and the pricing sign-off path so we can move to pilot. Priya, you good to confirm agenda?
[00:36] Priya: Yes, that's right. Procurement needs to see the final redlines and the pricing tiers. Also want to confirm any data residency constraints because we serve EU patients, so DPA particulars are huge.
[01:10] Maya: Great — we'll walk through the proposed redline doc. Liam will cover pilot and performance. Noah will list the security pack.
[01:45] Carlos: Quick flag from legal — indemnity language, specifically third-party claims and cap amount. We previously flagged 10x fees in our contract, and your MSA proposes unlimited for IP. That's a hard stop for us.
[02:20] Maya: Understood. The standard Redwood MSA has an IP indemnity carveout, but we can propose a reciprocal cap. Liam, remind me what the current default is?
[02:40] Liam: Default is liability cap at fees paid in prior 12 months, but for enterprise we sometimes do negotiated caps or carveouts for gross negligence. From a product stance, we can't accept unlimited IP indemnification.
[03:05] Carlos: Okay, attorney eyes are on that. We'll send language that keeps their platform indemnity limited; we may accept exceptions for willful misconduct.
[03:40] Jodie: On the technical side, two asks: 1) can Redwood offer BYOK/KMS integration? 2) we need assurances around KV cache persistence and any PII flushing for live requests. Our security team is strict.
[04:05] Liam: We support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments and in Dedicated with proper key wrapping. For hosted, we offer KMS integration with a bring-your-own-key path soon — but for the pilot we can do a dedicated pool with a customer key wrapped by our HSM, requires contractual KMS terms.
[04:40] Ben: That's good, but we need the exact KMS flow diagram. Also where are audit logs stored, retention, and who has access?
[05:10] Noah: We'll attach the KMS architecture diagram and the audit log policy. SOC2 section and penetration test summary included. I'll share a link right after the call.
[05:40] Priya: Back to pricing — procurement needs to understand commitment tiers and exit clauses. Finance wants a 3-month trial then default to 12 months with option to cancel with 30 days.
[06:05] Maya: We can propose a 3-month pilot as a paid evaluation that counts toward any future commit. Pricing tiers usually have step-down unit costs at 6 and 12 months. I'll put together a few options.
[06:40] Carlos: Also need data residency in the DPA: for EU patient data must remain in EU, deletion cert in 30 days. Our clients will require that.
[07:05] Liam: Technically we can pin routing to EU regions and disable cross-region fallback for the pilot. The deletion cert (we provide a deletion token) can be produced by our ingestion pipeline — we'll need to define the retention flow. There might be a slight latency tradeoff if we force strict regional routing.
[07:40] Jodie: Latency is a concern but not a showstopper. We care more about correctness and residency. We will accept a slight penalty if you can guarantee residency and tamper-evident deletion logs.
[08:15] Maya: Noted. We'll note that in the redline: add residency controls and deletion SLA 30 days with certificate.
[08:40] Priya: On SLA credits — procurement needs clear definitions: uptime, measurement method, credit formula. Have seen vague language before and it's caused delays.
[09:10] Liam: Our SLA is measured at the API layer per calendar month with rolling 7-day windows for incident detection, credits based on percentage of monthly fees. We can share the exact credit table.
[09:45] Carlos: Legal would want explicit remedies, and not a sole remedy clause that limits exclusive damages. Also need to align on service interruption definitions.
[10:15] Maya: We can be explicit: define outage as total inability to serve requests for X minutes across Y region. We'll propose specific thresholds and the credit matrix in the redline.
[10:45] Ben: Security ask: retention limits on logs that may contain PHI. We need to ensure logs are redacted within 7 days and that any storage is encrypted at rest with AES-256 and KMS keys.
[11:20] Noah: Our storage defaults to AES-256 and we can redact request-level logs on request. For the pilot we'll set log retention per Sable's policy. I'll add the redaction flow to the security doc.
[11:50] Priya: Regarding procurement workflow: once we get the final annotated MSA and pricing, we need two internal approvals: Legal signoff plus Finance PO. Typical timing here is 7–10 business days. Does that align?
[12:20] Maya: Yes that's typical. We'll try to compress by delivering clean redlines and pricing by 2026-03-12 so you can route to finance.
[12:50] Carlos: One wrinkle: our legal team wants a Mutual NDA addendum about derived models trained in pilot. We can't allow model weights to be trained on customer data without permission.
[13:20] Liam: Redwood does not train customer-specific models in hosted mode; we may cache short-term KV but we do not persist customer data for model training. We can add explicit DPA language prohibiting training on customer data.
[13:50] Jodie: Good — please add that clause. Also we need clarity on model version pinning during the pilot to ensure reproducibility.
[14:20] Maya: We'll propose a version pin in the pilot SOW and vendor repo references.
[14:50] Priya: Pricing approvals — two items: discounted pilot rate and enterprise commit discounts. Finance will want sample invoices and estimated monthly spend.
[15:20] Maya: I'll send a pricing spreadsheet showing pilot discount, 6-month and 12-month commit pricing, per-token and embedding costs, and estimated monthly spend at typical 10M token/month.
[15:50] Carlos: On indemnity, one last ask — carve out open source licensing claims. We prefer a mutual IP indemnity with a cap of 3x annual fees or a fixed cap.
[16:15] Maya: That's reasonable. We'll propose cap options in the redline and mark open source claims specifically.
[16:40] Ben: On on-prem/private deployment — if we go private later, what's the timeline and support needed? This affects our procurement because some stakeholders prefer on-prem for PHI.
[17:10] Liam: Private deploy typically needs 6–8 weeks for packaging and network validation, but for initial proof we can run a dedicated pool in our cloud region with VPC peering and dedicated keys. Migration path documented in SOW.
[17:45] Jodie: Can you provide a high-level runbook of steps? We need to present to infra.
[18:05] Liam: Yes, we'll include a runbook and lift-and-shift checklist.
[18:35] Priya: Any third-party subprocessor list? We need to understand downstream transfers.
[19:00] Noah: We'll include subprocessors with region and purpose and an egress data flow diagram.
[19:30] Carlos: A small transcription nit — the MSA references 'Subprocessor' but doesn't define 'processor' vs 'subprocessor' in the same way we do. We'll supply precise definitions.
[20:00] Maya: Good call, legal definitions can be harmonized.
[20:30] Priya: Timeline ask — if we get final redlines by Friday (2026-03-12), when will pilot start?
[20:50] Maya: If redlines and pricing are approved by 3/12, we can start pilot as early as 3/16 pending SOW and a short onboarding checklist. Pilot duration proposed: 30 days.
[21:20] Jodie: For acceptance criteria, we need throughput numbers and latency p95 under 400ms for short prompts, and reproducibility on set of eval prompts.
[21:50] Liam: We'll design a benchmark that includes 95th percentile latency and throughput. For reproducibility we'll pin model and seed prompts. We'll run a simulated workload that mirrors your traffic shape.
[22:20] Ben: Also add a security acceptance check: we require vulnerability scan results and access review during pilot.
[22:50] Noah: We'll share the pen-test summary and proposed timeline for interim scans.
[23:20] Carlos: About credits — we need to preserve the ability to seek equitable remedies beyond credits in case of gross negligence.
[23:45] Maya: We'll propose carveouts to the sole remedy clause so that gross negligence or willful misconduct isn't limited to financial credits.
[24:10] Priya: On data deletion, can Redwood provide a deletion certificate per dataset? Our processes need an auditable trail.
[24:40] Liam: Yes, we issue deletion certificates and can add a signed attestation. Expect a 30-day window for full pipeline purging in standard flow.
[25:05] Jodie: One oddball question — how do you handle model hallucinations and auditability? We need to trace input to response for remediation.
[25:35] Liam: We have request-level traces that map prompt, model version, and token-level generation metadata. For PHI we'll restrict access to that trace and redact as needed. We'll include retention policy.
[26:05] Maya: Closing loop — we'll produce an annotated MSA with proposed edits, a pricing spreadsheet with tiered options, the security pack (SOC2, pen-test), KMS diagram, and pilot SOW. Action items captured.
[26:40] Priya: Thank you. One more ask — can you include a simple procurement checklist noting typical internal approvers so we can speed routing?
[27:00] Maya: Yes — I'll include a one-page procurement checklist: Legal, Finance, Security, IT.
[27:20] Carlos: We'll aim to return MSA redlines by 3/15 if possible.
[27:40] Priya: Finance will try to approve PO by 3/16 if the numbers match expectation.
[28:00] Maya: Great. Liam, any technical clarifications before we wrap?
[28:15] Liam: Just one — for the pilot dataset, Ben, can you confirm size and whether it's synthetic or production-masked?
[28:30] Ben: We'll provide masked production slices — about 2M tokens per day over a 7-day window for the pilot.
[28:50] Liam: Got it. That helps set the throughput target.
[29:10] Maya: Ok team — we'll follow up with the docs and set a 30-minute legal redline review next week. Thanks all.

End of recording.
